prompt_md: Three friends play rock-paper-scissors, throwing at random. If exactly two kinds of throw show, the beaten drop out; otherwise replay. Average rounds until one is left?
prompt_short: Three-way rock-paper-scissors. Average rounds to one winner?
hint_md: After one round, are 3, 2 or 1 players left, and how likely is each?
explain_intuition_md: With two players a round settles things 2 times in 3, so 1.5 rounds is tempting. But with three players a round often knocks out only one person, leaving a two-player game that needs 1.5 more rounds on average. One round leaves three, two or one players with equal chances.
explain_math_md: Of 27 throws, 9 change nothing, 9 leave one winner and 9 leave two. With $E_2 = \tfrac32$: $$E_3 = 1 + \tfrac13E_3 + \tfrac13E_2 \;\Rightarrow\; E_3 = \tfrac94 = 2.25$$
